source: ADR-0071's re-founding table, 2026-08-11 (#326), superseding the human ruling on #258 as amended by #217 item 9
coverage: This table is not a complete account of what needs routing, and this sentence rides on a clear read as well as on a refusal, because the reader told nothing is wrong is the reader forming a belief about what was checked. Class 6 asserts an invariant no refusal enforces, and its path list names a minority of the gates this project runs; classes 4 and 5 refuse no route at all; class 3 is bound to a seat and so is checked at dispatch only, since a landing has no seat to check. A surface this file does not name is uncovered, never cleared, and a rung that did not run is not a rung that passed. Class ids 1 and 7 are retired by ADR-0071's re-founding table and are never reused, so an id is a stable historical handle rather than a position.

classes.name: orchestration
classes.label: Orchestration
classes.remedy: Keep orchestration on its Claude seat. This is the one provenance rule ADR-0071 ruling 1 left standing, and it is provisional: it says the seat deciding what everything else does should not move before a tested alternative exists, and it ends when the Codex orchestrator backup is built.

classes.name: adr_authorship
classes.label: ADR authorship
classes.remedy: Route ADR authorship to the three seats ADR-0071 rulings 2 and 4 require between them, on any lane including a foreign one: `planner` authors it, off the ordered profile preferences ruling 2 gives that seat; `implementer` lands it, because ruling 2's planner "neither gates nor lands"; and `review` reviews that landing, because ruling 4 lands no change alone. A row admitting the planner alone admitted nobody who could finish the work and refused the very review dispatch ruling 4 mandates — the deadlock found in review round 2, claim 1 — so the admitted set is the whole route rather than its first step. Every other seat is refused on every lane including Claude's: `recon` changes nothing, `orchestrator` is class 2's seat, `fable` survives only as #300's retro allowance, and `retro` files and lands nothing under ruling 3 — the retro half of the class this row descends from is withdrawn by that ruling, along with its `docs/process-log.md` path. That is what ruling 1 means by eligibility ceasing to be a property of provenance — a lane-selected refusal here would have refused `codex`/`codex-sol-xhigh`/`planner`, the first entry in the list this remedy prescribes, while clearing any Claude seat whatever. The class is therefore enforced where a seat exists, which is dispatch. `just land` is handed a lane and a diff and no seat, so this row carries no landing prefixes and the landing rung does not test it — an ADR reaching `origin/main` from an unappointed seat is uncaught, not cleared. **Flagged, not silently overridden (review round 2 claim 3): ADR-0071's re-founding table prescribes `docs/adr/` as this row's landing path, and this row has none.** A seat-bound row carrying landing prefixes would clear at dispatch for the seat it appoints and then refuse that same route at landing, where no seat is knowable, so the two cannot both hold as written; whether the ADR is amended or an ADR-0013 record covers the departure is the human's, and until one of those lands the conflict stands on the record rather than in a commit message.

classes.name: plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green
classes.label: The #181 shape
issue_phrases: plausible wrong fix would also have gone green
plausible wrong fix would also go green
classes.remedy: No mechanical gate distinguishes this diagnosis's plausible wrong fix from the right one, so the remedy is capability rather than provenance: route it to the `planner` seat and escalate. ADR-0071 ruling 5's fourth transferring-escalation condition, `plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green`, fires on exactly this class and names the transfer; the condition and its remedy are data in `config/escalation-conditions.json` and reach an agent as an emission.

classes.name: in_world_landings
classes.label: In-world landings
classes.remedy: A subagent cannot hold the full `just regress` corpus's foreground wait — `.claude/hooks/deny-subagent-waits.py` denies it — so a seat reached as a subagent cannot gate its own in-world work and must not take it. That is the whole of the rule: `just dispatch` launches a top-level session, which the wait hook permits by returning 0 where there is no agent id, so this row refuses no dispatch route. Its two path lists remain the one authority for what an in-world surface is, read by `just land`'s corpus rung, `tools/admission.py` and `tools/brief.py` (#302).

classes.name: gates_themselves
classes.label: The gates themselves
classes.remedy: Two rules live on this row and they are not the same rule, so read which one refused you. The **invariant** is the conflict of interest — no instance authors the gate that judges it — and it binds every instance, Claude's included; it is discharged by an independent review under ADR-0071 ruling 4, and **no refusal enforces it** until step 7's exemption list lands, so today it is asserted and honoured by procedure. The **refusal** you have actually met is the older keep-on-Claude bar, still selected by lane: a foreign lane is refused these paths and the Claude lane is exempt. It is kept, and the label kept with it, because retiring it before the exemption list exists would leave the gates with neither rule; it is not evidence that the invariant was checked, and a Claude landing here has cleared nothing. The half of the invariant that is enforceable today is enforced: this class carries no exception, and the withdrawn `Routing-exception: proposal-only` marker went with the framing, because an instance that can except itself from the gate that judges it is precisely the shape being forbidden. `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/settings.json` are here, not dropped: they are the denial layer and the permission allowlist, and the withdrawn gated-semantic-surfaces class was the only routing rule that named them. Coverage is incomplete: the list names six tools plus those two paths, and omits `tools/check_adr_form.py`, `tools/check_seat_config.py`, `tools/check_validated_markers.py`, `tools/check_conflict_markers.py`, `tools/check_source_symlink.py`, `tools/check_sqf_bans.py`, `tools/generate_seats.py` and `tools/export_command_schema.py` — the eight `just check` reaches — and `tools/breaker.py`, which no `check-*` recipe runs and which `just breaker` and `just watch-report` reach instead (review round 2 claim 4, correcting both this clause and ADR-0071's own row 6, which made the same slip) — along with every gate reached only through `just unit`, `just mutation`, `just land` and `just regress`. A diff touching a gate this list does not name is uncovered, never cleared.
